candidate_semantics.name: LineageAdmissionIdentity V1 candidate
candidate_semantics.purpose: Provide a domain-separated content binding for an admission statement that was independently admitted outside clonable Frank state.
candidate_semantics.expected_limitation: An exact copy of the same admission statement has the same content hash; anti-transplant therefore requires an independent boot-time trust input and freshness check.

external_primary_evidence.finding: machine-id and application-specific derivations provide stable local identifiers/privacy separation, not a non-clonable trust root; machine-id is read from persistent local state.

TPM2-backed material can be encrypted under a primary key derived from the TPM seed that is not permitted to leave the TPM, optionally PCR-bound; this is a materially stronger non-clonable-input candidate when a suitable TPM/vTPM is actually present.

Hostinger exposes account-authenticated VPS operations addressed by virtualMachineId, but this research pass found no primary documentation establishing a local cryptographic instance-attestation primitive available to the guest.

architecture_fusion.law: A verifier whose complete trusted input is cloned with the state cannot distinguish a perfect clone from the original when all observable inputs are equal; unique anti-transplant identity therefore needs at least one independently trusted, non-cloned input.
do_not_use_as_sole_anchor: root-owned file copied with the filesystem
DMI UUID without separate trust/attestation proof
candidate_anchor_order: TPM/vTPM-backed non-exportable secret or attested key, if present and validated on the accepted target
independent owner/provider admission service with anti-replay/freshness plus a non-cloned authentication factor
explicit operator-authorized migration/recovery receipt for legitimate body moves
architecture_fusion.open_target_question: Does the accepted Hostinger Ubuntu target expose a usable TPM/vTPM or another non-clonable guest-visible attestation primitive?
architecture_fusion.queued_read_only_probe: The accepted-target candidate workflow records TPM device presence, systemd-creds TPM2 capability, virtualization type, DMI readability and machine-id presence without emitting identifier values.

next_falsifier: When accepted-target execution is available, read the non-secret anchor capability inventory. If TPM/vTPM is absent, reject the TPM branch and design an external admission verifier with an independently held factor; if present, build the smallest TPM-backed challenge/anchor candidate and test clone/restart/rollback/migration controls without granting effect authority.
